high.title: August KTB Issuance Plan Points to Yield Curve Flattening
high.summary:
KB Securities analyst Ahn Jae-kyun forecasts a flattening of the 10-year to 3-year Korean Treasury Bond (KTB) yield curve, citing two key drivers: (1) rising probability of a policy rate hike at the Bank of Korea's August Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting, and (2) supply-side pressure concentrated in the 2-3 year segment of the KTB curve due to August issuance plans. The report, titled "Curve Strategy," suggests that monetary policy uncertainty will ease somewhat following the August BOK meeting, which could trigger a re-pricing across the front end of the curve. For KRW bond traders, the key takeaway is to position for a flatter curve — potentially fading any steepening trades in the 3s10s space ahead of the MPC. A BOK rate hike, if confirmed, would also be KRW-supportive in the near term, as higher rates relative to peers could attract foreign fixed-income inflows. Watch the August BOK meeting closely as the pivotal catalyst for both the rates and FX outlook.

---

high.title: US Treasury Joins Japan in Yen-Buying Intervention for First Time in Nearly 30 Years
high.summary: The United States and Japan conducted coordinated yen-buying intervention for the first time in approximately 30 years, marking an extraordinary development in G7 FX policy. The dollar-yen rate surged to the mid-160 level early in the New York session before rapidly reversing as speculation of U.S. involvement spread, with the pair falling sharply to the 153–154 range shortly after the intervention was confirmed. This is highly significant for KRW traders: coordinated G7 FX intervention sets a powerful precedent and signals that major economies are increasingly willing to defend currency values through direct market action. South Korea and Japan reportedly intervened simultaneously (as referenced in Article 4), suggesting a degree of regional coordination. For KRW, a stronger yen environment could reduce competitive depreciation pressure on the won, though any dollar-strengthening reversal could quickly erode those gains. Watch for follow-through yen stability, BOK commentary on intervention rationale, and whether the coordinated action shifts broader EM Asia FX sentiment toward stability.

high.title: NDF at 1,442.70/1,443.10 Won — Up 19.40 Won
high.summary: The dollar-won one-month NDF surged overnight in New York, with the mid-price quoted at 1,442.90 won — representing a sharp 19.40 won jump from the previous Seoul spot close of 1,424.00 won. The bid/ask spread was tight at 1,442.70 / 1,443.10, suggesting active and liquid offshore positioning. This NDF print is a critical leading indicator for the Seoul onshore open, implying the won could gap significantly weaker at the start of the next trading session. The 19-won move is a substantial single-session shift and reflects a rapid unwinding of the intervention-driven won strength, compounded by geopolitical risk premium (Iran strike fears) and global risk-off flows. For KRW traders, this signals elevated volatility at the open and potential for further weakness if geopolitical risks escalate. The BOK's tolerance for this level of depreciation — and whether they re-enter the market — will be the key variable to monitor intraday.

high.title: Won Rises to Mid-1,430s Amid Weekend Iran Strike Warnings
high.summary: The dollar-won exchange rate climbed to the mid-1,430 won level as the post-intervention rally in the won was reversed by multiple headwinds. Reports that the U.S. and Israel could strike Iran's energy facilities as early as the weekend triggered a flight to safe-haven assets and broad emerging market currency weakness. The sharp appreciation seen immediately after South Korea and Japan's coordinated FX intervention was partially unwound during the session, with the won giving back gains. Notably, the yen re-strengthened on caution over potential further U.S. intervention, providing some relative support. For KRW positioning, this article highlights the tug-of-war between intervention-driven support and geopolitical risk-off pressure. Energy-importing Korea is particularly exposed to oil price shocks from Middle East escalation, which would simultaneously pressure the current account and the won. Traders should monitor oil prices, weekend geopolitical developments, and any BOK communication regarding FX tolerance levels heading into the new week.

high.title: South Korean Bond Futures Fall on U.S. Treasury Weakness — 10-Year Down 23 Ticks
high.summary: South Korean government bond futures declined in overnight trading, closely tracking weakness in U.S. Treasuries. The 3-year KGB futures contract closed at 103.18, down 5 ticks from the prior regular session close, while the 10-year contract fell 23 ticks — a more pronounced move reflecting duration-sensitive selling. Foreign investors were net sellers of 122 contracts in the 3-year futures, while domestic financial investment firms and retail investors provided partial offsetting demand (net buyers of 51 and 78 contracts, respectively). The foreign net selling is noteworthy in the context of broader EM capital outflow risks and elevated global yields. With U.S. Treasury yields driving the move, Korean bonds remain highly correlated to global rate dynamics. For bond investors, the 23-tick drop in 10-year futures suggests rising yield pressure at the long end. Key watch points: direction of U.S. Treasuries, BOK rate path expectations following the upcoming release of July 16 MPC minutes, and whether foreign selling in futures escalates into the cash bond market.

high.title: US and Israel Prepare to Strike Iranian Energy Facilities 'As Early as This Weekend' (Breaking)
high.summary: A CBS report indicates the United States and Israel could strike Iranian energy infrastructure — including power plants and refineries — as early as this weekend. While the article is brief, the geopolitical implications for Korean financial markets are significant and warrant close monitoring.

high.title: Korean Government Bonds Rally on WGBI Demand Hopes Despite KOSPI Surge — 3-Year Yield Down 5.2bp
high.summary:
South Korean government bond yields declined across the board on July 31st, with the benchmark 3-year yield falling 5.2 basis points, as two key catalysts converged. First, the government signaled a commitment to stabilizing long-term rates through its August treasury bond issuance plan released after the previous session's close — a move interpreted as supply-side support for the bond market. Second, and more significantly, investor focus was squarely on anticipated demand tied to Korea's inclusion in the FTSE World Government Bond Index (WGBI), with month-end rebalancing flows expected to drive meaningful foreign inflows into KTBs.

Notably, this bond rally occurred despite the KOSPI surging nearly 17% intraday — a rare decoupling that underscores how powerful the WGBI inclusion narrative is for fixed income markets. For international bond investors, this is a critical signal: passive index-tracking demand may provide a durable technical bid for Korean government bonds in the near term. Watch for the magnitude of actual foreign inflows at month-end settlement and any Ministry of Economy and Finance guidance on issuance volumes, as these will be key drivers of yield direction heading into August.

high.title: [FX] Won Rebounds to Early 1,430s Amid Lack of Export Settlements and Bargain Buying
high.summary:
The USD/KRW exchange rate reversed an overnight sharp decline on July 31st, recovering from an intraday low of 1,423.90 won to trade around 1,432.80 won as of 11:17 a.m. Seoul time — representing a net decline of 4.60 won from the prior session close of 1,437.40 won. The pair opened at 1,424.20 won before steadily paring losses throughout the morning session.

The key driver of the rebound appears to be a lack of export settlement flows, which would typically provide USD supply and support the won. Additionally, bargain buying of the dollar at lower levels provided a technical floor. For KRW traders, this price action highlights a tug-of-war between structural won-supportive factors (WGBI inflows, KOSPI rally) and the absence of sufficient export-side USD selling. The 1,423–1,424 zone is emerging as a near-term support for USD/KRW, while the 1,437–1,440 band represents overhead resistance. Watch export settlement timing and foreign equity/bond inflow data closely as potential catalysts for the next directional move.

high.title: Gundlach Says US Long-Term Rates Could Hit Mid-5% Range by Next FOMC
high.summary: Jeffrey Gundlach, CEO of DoubleLine Capital and one of the most closely watched fixed income voices globally, projected that U.S. long-term interest rates could climb to the mid-5% range by the September FOMC meeting. This forecast came amid the Fed holding its federal funds rate target range at 3.50–3.75%, though notably three policy members dissented in favor of a rate hike — signaling meaningful hawkish pressure within the Committee.

medium.title: Japan's MOF Says It Has Means to Secure Dollars, Including Borrowing Against US Treasuries
medium.summary: Japan's Ministry of Finance publicly signaled its capacity to conduct large-scale yen-buying, dollar-selling FX intervention by highlighting its ability to borrow against US Treasury holdings in cooperation with US authorities. The announcement, disseminated via X (formerly Twitter) in both English and Japanese, appears designed to enhance the credibility and deterrence effect of potential BOJ/MOF intervention operations. For KRW/USD traders, this is regionally significant: aggressive JPY intervention that strengthens the yen could generate spillover appreciation pressure on the KRW, as both currencies tend to move in tandem during broad dollar-weakening episodes. Additionally, a stronger yen narrative may shift regional capital flows and influence BOK's own intervention calculus. Monitor USD/JPY levels and any follow-through BOJ action as a leading indicator for KRW direction.

medium.title: Next Week's Schedule for Ministry of Finance and Economy and Other Economic Ministries
medium.summary: The Korean government's economic calendar for the week of August 3–6 includes several market-relevant data releases. Most critically, **July 2026 Consumer Price Index (CPI) data** is scheduled for release on Tuesday, August 5 at 08:00, alongside a Price-Related Vice Ministers' Meeting — signaling elevated official attention to inflation dynamics. The CPI print will be a key input for the BOK's August MPC deliberations on the policy rate. A higher-than-expected inflation reading could reinforce the case for tightening flagged by KB Securities (see above), steepening expectations for a rate hike and providing near-term KRW support. Bond markets should brace for potential volatility around the CPI release, particularly at the front end of the KTB curve. Also note the Deputy Prime Minister's Cabinet Meeting on August 4, which may yield policy guidance relevant to fiscal and economic conditions.

medium.title: South Korean Financial Regulators Weekly Schedule — Aug 3–7
medium.summary:
This week's regulatory calendar contains two high-priority data releases for market participants. On **Wednesday August 6 at 06:00**, the BOK will publish **foreign exchange reserves as of end-July 2026** — a closely watched figure that will reveal the scale of any intervention during the recent coordinated Korea-Japan FX action. A significant drawdown in reserves would confirm the extent of BOK market participation and signal its FX defense commitment. On **Tuesday August 5 at 16:00**, the **Minutes of the 13th Monetary Policy Board meeting (July 16)** will be released, offering crucial insights into the BOK's rate deliberations, growth and inflation assessments, and any internal debate on the policy path. Given current won weakness and global yield pressures, these minutes could meaningfully shift rate expectations and KGB yields. Both releases are must-watch events for KRW and bond traders this week.

---

medium.title: Conflicting Investor Flows Double Market Volatility in South Korean Stocks
medium.summary:
A report from the Korea Capital Market Institute identifies conflicting trading patterns among different investor types as the primary driver of elevated equity market volatility in Korea this year, with domestic volatility exceeding that of major peer markets. The four empirically identified drivers suggest structural rather than purely cyclical forces are at play. For fund managers, elevated equity volatility can spill into FX markets, as heightened uncertainty tends to amplify KRW volatility via risk-off flows and foreign investor repositioning. This is relevant context for sizing KRW and KOSPI positions, particularly given the current global macro backdrop. Monitoring foreign investor net flows on the KOSPI remains important as a leading indicator for KRW direction.

---

medium.title: KOSPI Surges 1,000 Points in Single Day, Shattering Multiple Records
medium.summary: While individual equity market movements are generally outside the core brief scope, the magnitude of this event carries meaningful implications for KRW and capital flow dynamics. The KOSPI reportedly surged over 1,000 points in a single session — the largest percentage gain and point increase in history. Crucially, foreign investors recorded their largest-ever single-session net buying, while retail investors posted their largest-ever net selling. This extreme foreign inflow surge is directly relevant to KRW demand dynamics, as large-scale equity-related FX conversion from foreign buyers would provide significant near-term support for the Won. Fund managers should monitor whether this foreign buying momentum is sustained or represents a one-day spike, and watch for any associated KRW appreciation pressure or BOK smoothing operations in the FX market in subsequent sessions.

medium.title: President Lee to Hold Closed-Door Meeting on Real Estate and Stock Markets Upon Return
medium.summary: President Lee Jae-myung is returning from an 11-day overseas tour and will immediately convene a closed-door meeting to address domestic economic concerns, including real estate market instability and sharp stock market fluctuations. Policy uncertainty around tax and capital market regulations has reportedly generated market controversy during his absence. While details remain sparse, any policy signals emerging from this meeting — particularly around capital gains taxation, financial transaction rules, or real estate-related credit measures — could have downstream implications for Korean bond markets, banking sector sentiment, and KRW stability. Investors should watch for official statements post-briefing on the 3rd–4th.

medium.title: BOJ Holds Key Rate at 1%; Takata Dissents with Call for Hike
medium.summary: The Bank of Japan maintained its benchmark interest rate at 1.0% following its July 31st two-day policy meeting, with the decision passing 8-1. The sole dissenter, board member Hajime Takata, advocated for a hike to 1.25%, arguing the BOJ has entered a new phase requiring further normalization. While this is a Japan-focused event, it carries meaningful spillover implications for Korean markets. A more hawkish BOJ trajectory would likely support JPY strength, which historically pressures KRW through export competitiveness channels and risk sentiment in Asian FX. Additionally, any shift in Japanese investor yield-seeking behavior — particularly a repatriation of capital from Korean bonds — could affect demand dynamics in the KTB market. The Takata dissent keeps the door open for a BOJ hike at subsequent meetings; traders should monitor subsequent BOJ communications closely for guidance on the pace of normalization and its impact on USD/JPY and, by extension, USD/KRW cross dynamics.

medium.title: [Table] Interbank Short-term Interest Rate Benchmark — KORIBOR (July 31st)
medium.summary: This data release provides the Korea Inter-bank Offered Rates (KORIBOR) as announced by Yonhap Infomax at 11:00 a.m. on July 31st. KORIBOR serves as a key benchmark for short-term interbank lending in Korea and is a useful real-time gauge of domestic liquidity conditions and market expectations around Bank of Korea policy. While the article content does not include the specific rate levels, traders should cross-reference the published figures against recent trends to identify any tightening or easing in short-term funding conditions, particularly in the context of BOK's rate trajectory and the broader bond market rally observed on the same day.

medium.title: Samsung Electronics Foreign Ownership Hits 16-Year Low — 'Underweighting Excessive'
medium.summary: Samsung Electronics' foreign ownership ratio has fallen to its lowest level since 2010, with the MSCI EM Index weighting gap between Samsung and TSMC narrowing to its smallest since 2015. Securities firms are flagging the underweighting as excessive, suggesting a potential mean-reversion opportunity. While this is primarily an equity story, the persistent reduction in foreign holdings of Korea's largest-cap stock reflects broader capital outflow trends that weigh on the KRW. A reversal in foreign positioning — should sentiment shift — could provide a meaningful tailwind for both the KOSPI and the Korean won. Fund managers tracking Korea equity/FX correlation should monitor foreign net buying data on Samsung as a leading indicator of broader EM re-allocation into Korea.

medium.title: President Lee Returns from Overseas Trip to Face Domestic Challenges — Stock Market, Real Estate 'Pile of Problems'
medium.summary: President Lee Jae-myung returns on August 3rd following an 11-day overseas trip covering the U.S. and Latin America, where he advanced AI cooperation and critical mineral supply chain deals. However, the article notes that domestic stock market and real estate conditions deteriorated during his absence, framing the political backdrop as challenging. For KRW and Korean asset traders, the political risk premium and the government's capacity to implement market-supportive measures warrant monitoring. Any fiscal or regulatory response to domestic market weakness could influence near-term sentiment for Korean equities and indirectly support KRW stability.
